antagonism

/an-TAG-uh-niz-um/ - the stress falls on TAG · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Antagonism means active hostility between people.

The antagonism between the upstairs and downstairs tenants began over a parking spot and now runs through every building meeting.

Example

The two star surgeons' antagonism split the hospital into camps: nurses learned never to praise one in the other's operating room, and residents chose sides by their second week.

Antagonism names active, two-sided hostility that has become the relationship itself. Friction is a passing rub between people who otherwise get along; hatred can be one-sided and hidden; antagonism takes two, and it shows — in vetoes, snubs, and seating charts.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

animus: Animus is the formal word for settled ill feeling toward someone — a lawyer's or editorial writer's term — and it can stay quietly one-sided. Antagonism takes two and shows itself in vetoes, snubs, and open opposition. A judge may harbor animus no one ever detects; antagonism is visible to the whole room.

opposition: Opposition is resistance to a person or plan, and it can be entirely respectful — colleagues oppose each other's budgets and still share lunch. Antagonism adds hostility: the resistance has turned personal and mutual, a standing state of bad blood rather than a mere difference of position.

enmity: Enmity is the deep, settled state of being enemies, and it can smolder in silence for years without one public act. Antagonism is enmity in motion — active, two-sided hostility that everyone can watch. Enemies who never cross paths still hold enmity; rivals sniping in every joint meeting show antagonism.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

goodwill: friendly, cooperative feeling toward someone

friendliness: open warmth in everyday dealings

Where it sits · how deeply the bad blood runs

friction → antagonism → hatred

friction vs. antagonism: Friction is a passing rub between people who mostly get along — milder than antagonism, which is hostility as a standing relationship.

hatred vs. antagonism: Hatred goes further than antagonism: beyond opposing someone at every turn, it consumes the one who feels it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ant-: against (a form of anti-)

Root — agon: struggle, contest (Greek)

Suffix — -ism: state or condition

Put it together: Ant- (against) + agon (contest) + -ism (state) = the state of struggling against someone. Greek agon was the arena contest itself; antagonism keeps that picture — two opponents circling, the struggle hardened into a standing condition.

Use the root in a new word: agony: Fans called the penalty shootout agony to watch.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / analytic

Antagonism is the standing condition of mutual hostility — use it for relationships, not moments. A single hostile act shows aggression; rancor (this unit) is the bitter feeling one side nurses in private; antagonism is the two-way state of war, visible to everyone.
